question: Can edge-tts make a letter's SOUND (a sustained sss) rather than its NAME (ess)?
method: Render each candidate, then segment the first word by zero-crossing rate: S = unvoiced hiss (/s/), V = voiced (any vowel), durations in seconds. A sustained sss is one unbroken S. The letter name 'ess' is V then S. 'ess ess ess' is V S V S V S. Measured with `npm run voice:inspect`; nobody on this end could listen.
verdict: No spelling produces a sustained /s/. edge-tts reads every run of s's as the letter NAME, once per letter. SSML is escaped by the package and read aloud as literal tags. Voiced continuants (m) do sustain, because 'Mmm' is a lexicalised interjection rather than a letter run.

authoringRuleForNow: Voiced continuants (m, n, l, r, v, z, and the vowels) can be authored as the doubled interjection spelling and will sustain: 'Mmm' gives 0.36s of unbroken hum with no letter name. Unvoiced consonants cannot; author them as 'Suh'-style approximations, accept the schwa, and revisit every one of them when ElevenLabs lands.
